page: OVHcloud l4-90 is a GPU-accelerated server belonging to the Cloud GPU family. It features 22 dedicated physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 9454 processor running at 2.75 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 90.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.09 GB per core, alongside a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. Acceleration is driven by a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Network connectivity is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in specific compute and memory metrics. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng ranks in the top 10%, while multi-core performance is strong, placing in the top 25%. Passmark memory testing also achieves a top-tier rating. In LLM inference workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier efficiency, processing prompts and generating text at high speeds for small (135M) and medium (7B) models. However, memory bandwidth for large blocks and standard database operations perform within average ranges, indicating a tradeoff where raw compute and GPU-driven tasks outperform standard memory-throughput-heavy operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the l4-90 offers a balanced resource density by pairing dedicated AMD EPYC cores with a modern Ada Lovelace GPU, avoiding the higher costs associated with larger multi-GPU systems. This profile makes the server highly suitable for machine learning inference, image processing, and physics simulations. It is also well-suited for workloads requiring dedicated CPU threads and moderate local NVMe storage, such as specialized data processing and medium-scale AI model deployment.
